processing: A green tea blending traditional methods with modern ones, in a range running from Gongcha through Cuiya, Wuya and Maofeng to wild-leaf green. Details of the method are not widely published.
harvest_season: Little is documented for this tea; as with other Sichuan greens, spring tea is the prized picking.
appearance_dry: Tight, even strips with a frosted grey-green colour.
appearance_wet: Little is documented; expect green leaf in the manner of other strip greens.
taste_profile: Strong, clean and fresh with a mellow body and a sweet finish, in the manner of high-mountain tea.

brewing.notes: General advice for strip-shaped greens: a little hotter than for bud teas, with short steeps so the stronger taste does not turn bitter.

vintage_note: As usual for a Chinese green, it is sold from the current year's harvest and best drunk within the year. The range has several product names, so check which grade you are buying and the harvest date.
description:
Luming Gongcha is a mountain green from Gong County in Yibin, in southern Sichuan near the Yunnan border. Gongcha means tribute tea, and the name is more a historical claim than a description of the leaf.

The county is limestone mountain country, rising to more than 1,600 metres. The modern tea was developed by the Yongxing tea farm with a university, and comes in a range of named grades.

The usual description is tight frosted grey-green strips and a bright yellow-green cup, with a strong, clean, mellow taste and a sweet finish. Slightly hotter water works, as long as you keep it short.

Look for the protected name and a recent harvest. The word wild on a pack is worth asking about, as it is a marketing-friendly term.
history:
Local accounts say that tea from Gong County received the Luming tribute name in 771, during the Tang dynasty. This is a promotional claim that is hard to check, and it should be read as tradition.

The tea as sold today dates from the 1990s, when the Yongxing tea farm and Sichuan Agricultural University's tea and horticulture college developed it together. National geographical indication protection came in March 2018, covering the whole county.
